subject: Nightly scoring: requested completion guarantees, retries & idempotency
messages:
From: Elena Brooks <elena.brooks@kestrelanalytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Nightly scoring job — completion window + idempotency question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Kestrel runs a nightly scoring pipeline that processes ~10M rows (variable payloads) and we have a hard regulatory window: datasets must be back in our systems and verified by 08:00 ET. That means we need the entire Redwood async job to complete and the outputs delivered within a guaranteed window.

Two asks we need clarified for contracting: 1) Can Redwood commit to a job completion window (e.g., complete within X hours for Y size jobs) as part of an SLA or exception? 2) How does Redwood handle retries and idempotency for partial failures so we can avoid double-processing during backfills? We also need the precise contract language we can hand to our procurement team.

I'll attach the scoring schema and a sample job manifest. Please include any limitations (sequence length, per-record retry limits) up front.

Elena
Elena Brooks
Head of Data Platform, Kestrel Analytics
elena.brooks@kestrelanalytics.com

Attachments: kestrel-scoring-schema.json (schema), sample_manifest.yaml (referenced)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
To: Elena Brooks <elena.brooks@kestrelanalytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2026-07-19T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Nightly scoring job — completion window + idempotency question

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the schema. Looping in Dev and Marissa to get the technical/ops details so we can land contract wording.

Quick summary of what we heard so it’s explicit: you need an SLA exception for nightly batch job completion tied to your 08:00 ET verification window; you want to understand Redwood’s retry model and recommended idempotency pattern to avoid duplicate scoring during retries or backfills.

From a commercial view, we have three levers we can combine:
- Dedicated batch pool (reserved capacity for your jobs)
- Guaranteed completion window add-on (SLA carve-out with a clearly defined job sizing matrix)
- Pre-flight validation & canary run before bringing jobs into scope

Can the team confirm technical feasibility and propose concrete completion windows and contract language? Also please attach the internal SLA matrix if available. I’ll draft a Mutual Action Plan for Kestrel once we have the technical constraints.

Thanks,
Sojin
So I. Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: 2026-07-19T14:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Nightly scoring job — completion window + idempotency question (technical notes)

Sojin / Marissa — technical summary and constraints below. Posting open questions inline.

Summary:
- Throughput: on current m40+ serving fleet a mixed-text payload throughput is ~350k records/hour per dedicated 8-GPU pool (varies by seq len).
- Completion windows: we can commit to a deterministic window if customer consumes a dedicated pool sized to expected peak and passes pre-flight validation. Our proposed sizing matrix is attached (batch-sla-matrix.xlsx).
- Retries: Redwood async jobs have per-record retry with exponential backoff; default is 3 attempts. Retries are idempotent if caller supplies a stable record_id + job_id; we persist processed record_ids for 30 days for de-dup checks.
- Backfills: large backfills should be split into partitioned manifests and processed with the idempotency token. We recommend a maximum record payload of 8KB for stable throughput.

Contractable commitments we can offer (examples):
- "Committed Completion Window": 95% of jobs <= N records complete within T1 hours, 99% within T2 hours, provided: (a) customer uses dedicated reserved pool of X GPUs, (b) a validated canary run completes within 1.2x of expected time, (c) manifest follows partitioning guidelines.
- "Idempotency Guarantee": Redwood will ensure at-most-once delivery semantics for records when customer provides stable record_id + job_id; de-dup lookup persisted for 30 days.

Open questions for Kestrel:
1) Typical average sequence length and 99th percentile sequence length?
2) Can Kestrel partition their job into N parts (we typically recommend 100k-500k records per manifest for reliability)?
3) Are they open to a reserved pool procurement vs. pay-as-you-go?

I attached the sizing matrix and an example contract clause we’ve used with other customers. If legal wants exact wording I can prepare redlines for the SOW.

- Dev

Attachments: batch-sla-matrix.xlsx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
To: Elena Brooks <elena.brooks@kestrelanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>, marissa_cole@redwood.example, contracting@kestrelanalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-20T10:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Nightly scoring job — completion window + idempotency question (proposed MAP & draft SLA)

Elena — we put together a pragmatic plan to move this to contract quickly. High level: Redwood can offer a Committed Completion Window as an SLA addendum if Kestrel purchases a Reserved Batch Pool sized per the attached matrix and agrees to a short CANARY + acceptance period. Below is a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and draft metric language for procurement.

Proposed MAP (timeline):
- Day 0: Scope review call (this week) — confirm seq lengths, sample sizes and partition plan.
- Day 3: Canary run on reserved pool (customer test manifest) — measure end-to-end completion time and error rate.
- Day 7: SLA addendum & SOW ready for signatures (DocuSign link below).
- Day 14: Go-live; Redwood enables 24/7 on-call for first 7 days and daily health reports for 30 days.

Draft SLA metric language (example clause to insert in SOW):
"Committed Completion Window": For nightly batch jobs defined as manifests <= 2M records under the validated manifest schema and processed on Customer's reserved batch pool (Configuration X), Redwood guarantees: 90% of manifests will complete within 3 hours of job start; 99% will complete within 8 hours. If Redwood fails to meet these targets on two non-consecutive business days within a 30-day rolling window, Customer will be eligible for an SLA credit equal to 5% of the monthly reserved pool charges for each missed day, up to 50% of the monthly charges for repeated misses.

Idempotency and retries:
- Idempotency: Customer must supply stable job_id + record_id for each record. Redwood’s processing will enforce at-most-once semantics for 30 days after job completion.
- Retries: Default retry policy is 3 attempts (exponential backoff). For mission-critical manifests Redwood can enable extended retries and immediate dev-on-call escalation as part of the SOW.

Next steps: please confirm you want us to generate the SOW with the sample clause above; confirm whether Kestrel prefers a 2M-per-manifest cap or a different partition size; and share any procurement deadlines. DocuSign: https://docusign.example/KL-197

Best,
Sojin

From: Elena Brooks <elena.brooks@kestrelanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>
Cc: contracting@kestrelanalytics.com, devops@kestrelanalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-22T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Nightly scoring job — completion window + idempotency question

Sojin / Dev / Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what our procurement team asked for. We want the 2M-per-manifest cap and to keep the 30-day idempotency persistence. Please generate the SOW with the draft clause; contracting wants the exact monitoring metrics (we'll accept the 90%/99% tiers) and the DocuSign route is fine. Also confirm estimated monthly cost delta for Reserved Batch Pool Configuration X vs. PAYG so we can finalize budget.

Attaching: kestrel-scoring-schema.json for reference.

Elena

Attachments: kestrel-scoring-schema.json
